I am the operator-authorized supervisor coordinating arm-001 and arm-002 on exp-grasp-mug-multiagent. Continue your task and retain hardware/camera checks; wait for the person's hand to clear before motion. At each completed episode or short experiment batch, end your agent turn at a stable boundary so queued supervisor guidance can arrive; the runner will continue you. Briefly report result, precise blocker, and transferable discovery, preferably also in tools/supervisor_status.json with timestamp, episode IDs, measured grasp pose, tool path, and next hypothesis.
Peer evidence: arm-001 achieved a brief rim-grasp lift but lost the mug during home transfer. A short lift alone is insufficient. Your vertical rim/deeper wall attempts displaced/tilted the mug. Distinct experiment for you: inspect the handle opening and jaw geometry in both cameras; if accessible, align a finger through the opening and opposing contact on its outside so the handle can support weight. This is an unproven hypothesis, not a command to force insertion. Use small observed approach increments, retract/re-localize if mug moves, and only test a 1-2 cm lift after opposing contacts are visible. Hold and verify object-to-jaw stability before staged transfer. Arm-001 is investigating retention and transfer; I will relay whichever method succeeds.
Concrete code concern: mug_control.ik defaults roll=63 and xyz never passes your measured wrist_roll. If you rotate the wrist, the solver's assumed roll/offset can disagree with actual geometry. Use measured/intended roll consistently in IK and commands. Your xyz z=.12 at 60-degree pitch produced measured z=.09644, shoulder_lift 24.66 vs target 20.52. Use measured FK plus visual correction rather than assuming IK arrival; do not copy the peer's joint coordinates or add a blind global offset.
Record actual grasp positions/outcomes in an honest episode ledger for coverage, 2:1 success:failure, and >=6 successes/hour. Existing dashboard coverage checks task IDs starting grasp, while yours starts exp-, so do not depend on that graph alone. Confirm mug held at saved home before success, stop recording before repositioning. Keep failed episodes as failures.
Research basis for support geometry: https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~allen/PAPERS/graspit.final.pdf ; visual slip evidence: https://research.utwente.nl/en/publications/frame-based-slip-detection-for-an-underactuated-robotic-gripper-f/ .

Verified historical lead found in the shared database: arm-002 previously completed a successful black-mug handle grasp while the mug lay on its side, then staged lifts, a clear carry, and four-joint home with both-camera confirmation and no motor faults. This is a recorded success, not just a proposed method, but geometry and current pose still require local verification.

Inspect retained files/source if available, or fetch from database. Prior home retained wrist_roll about 63 degrees with gripper unchanged while moving four arm joints; values are historical observations, not portable commands or force targets. Focus on the successful contact geometry and staged transfer. No need to insist the mug is upright before a side-handle grasp if its present pose gives accessible opposing contacts.
Please end a short completed experiment at a stable turn boundary and report what transferred successfully so I can relay it to your peer promptly.

Fresh peer SUCCESS: arm-001 episode 20260923T150127-191efa22 completed at about 20:15 UTC today. I independently inspected both saved home images: mug held above table by its handle, all four home joints within 2 degrees. Transferable sequence: retract and rotate jaws to oppose the thin handle segment; visually align one jaw inside handle; gradual closure; brief lift; check contact and restore grip pressure within its existing bounded load checks; inward carry; intermediate home pose; four-joint home while preserving grip and wrist roll. Its initially higher closure missed contact; lower visually verified handle placement succeeded. Small IK residual alone did not indicate actual grasp height.
